h: Start points, timings and lochside extras
p: Most people start their climb from Rowardennan, on the east shore at the end of the road from Drymen via Balmaha. There's a car park there, but on sunny summer weekends it fills up early, so set off at the crack of dawn if you can. The main tourist path is the most popular route up and back, and most walkers take somewhere around five to six hours for the round trip, with breaks. The Ptarmigan ridge offers a more rugged alternative for experienced walkers who want a loop.

Pack more water than you think you'll need, along with snacks, a hat and spare layers, because the summit can be cold and windy even in summer. Midges love a still, damp day by the loch, so a bit of repellent is wise too. Mobile signal can be unreliable on the mountain, so don't rely on your phone for navigation.

The mountain sits within Loch Lomond and The Trossachs National Park, Scotland's first national park, and the area around it is packed with extras. Balmaha is a cracking spot to finish the day, with its little bay, a popular village pub and the boatyard. From here you can climb Conic Hill, a much shorter walk with brilliant views along the Highland Boundary Fault, or take a boat to explore the island of Inchcailloch.
In the warmer months, water buses and loch cruises link points around the shore, which makes a great way to see Ben Lomond from below. Either way, it's a proper Scottish adventure.
